extracted.intended_audience: Canadian government officials, provincial/municipal governments, and civil society organizations involved in preparing or implementing OGP national action plans
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, publishing, consulting on, and reporting national action plans under the Open Government Partnership, with priorities and standards for what makes plans successful and how progress should be tracked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to publish national action plans
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of OGP membership, countries are required to publish national action plans on open government to be implemented over a two-year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action plans must include specific commitments for advancing OGP principles across the country; publication is a membership obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-year implementation period for action plans
rubrics_metrics.description: National action plans are to be implemented over a two-year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should be structured and timed to cover a two-year implementation horizon (e.g., Canada's biennial plans).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific, time-bound, measurable commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Action plans must contain specific, time-bound and measurable commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful commitments are concrete and measurable; example: Canada's Third Biennial Plan (2016–2018) included 22 commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on significant national priorities and ambitious reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful plans focus on significant national open government priorities and ambitious reforms and are relevant to the values of transparency, accountability and public participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reforms that address nationally significant open-government challenges rather than trivial or purely procedural items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reporting on implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries must report publicly on implementing their national plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should be transparent and frequent; Canada goes beyond OGP annual self-assessments by providing a quarterly open government commitment progress tracker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public consultations in plan and self-assessment development
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries must complete public consultations in developing both national action plans and self-assessment reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultations should be robust and inclusive, engaging citizens and civil society early in the policy/process design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steering Committee composition and co-chair structure
rubrics_metrics.description: OGP is governed by a Steering Committee comprised of 11 government officials and 11 civil society representatives, led by four co-chairs: one lead government, one lead civil society organization, one supporting government and one supporting civil society organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting co-chairs are typically incoming co-chairs who serve one year as supporting co-chair and then the following year as lead co-chair; reflects parity between government and civil society in governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open data implementation and performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Open data is a core component of open government work; countries are assessed on implementation of open data efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance can be measured via international indices (e.g., Open Data Barometer); Canada ranked second in 2016. Open-data actions should be aligned with broader transparency commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results and delivery: demonstrate measurable impact and use trackers
rubrics_metrics.description: OGP and citizens expect measurable results; progress tracking and timely updates help demonstrate delivery on commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move beyond reporting counts (number of datasets or consultations) toward demonstrable outcomes; use tools such as a quarterly progress tracker to provide updates more frequently than annual self-assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intergovernmental engagement and harmonization
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to engaging sub-national governments to harmonize approaches to open data across jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include piloting a federated open-data search service and working with provinces/municipalities to align standards and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust, early-stage consultation and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitments should include robust consultations at the earliest stages of major policy reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early engagement with citizens and stakeholders in major policy areas (e.g., defence, international development, Arctic policy) is recognized as good practice by OGP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — Inclusion (openness beyond publishing data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Openness means being more than just publishing data and information; it requires being open to different cultures and people, a diversity of views and new ways of thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design plans and consultations to reach diverse communities and perspectives, not only technically accessible audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — Participation (access and diverse participation channels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government belongs to the people; citizens, civil society and businesses should have access to public data and a wide variety of ways to participate in government decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide multiple participation channels and ensure data/access enables meaningful public contribution and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — Impact (demonstrable, citizen-relevant outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The open government movement must demonstrate real, measurable results that affect citizens' day-to-day lives rather than relying only on counts of datasets or consultations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design commitments and monitoring to show outcomes and impacts that are understandable and relevant to citizens to sustain the movement.
